Children develop within distinct but interconnected contexts: their families, their schools, and the broader social and structural systems around them. Drawing on ecological systems theory and interdisciplinary perspectives, I study how these contexts shape children's learning, development, and access to educational opportunity, and how these processes vary across children and communities. This work grounds my partnership research: understanding the contexts children grow up in helps identify where systems can best support them.
